title: Mistral model resolution lacks response-body and read-time bounds
summary: The default mutable Mistral model alias triggers an authenticated model-list request whose response has no effective read or overall deadline and no body ceiling before JSON materialization. A connected service or intermediary can hang the command or consume substantial transient resources before OCR begins.

severity.rationale: The connected remote peer is a realistic in-scope attacker source on the default approved path. Impact is local availability rather than compromise, and the required matrix maps medium impact plus high likelihood to medium.
severity.changeConditions: Severity would rise if the default path produces persistent or broader service loss; it would fall after the configured deadline and response-byte ceilings are enforced or if supported configurations always use immutable model pins.

confidence.rationale: bounded configuration test+V10. Exact default-alias-to-GET-to-into_json source trace. Cargo.lock pins ureq 2.12.1; local primary source shows connect=30s, read/write/overall=None and unbounded serde_json::from_reader. Bounded network-free r12_2_timeout_seconds_non_default_is_loud_rejected test passed, confirming 30 is rejected and the unwired default 300 accepted.

taxonomy.category: remote response resource exhaustion / missing deadline (CWE-400, CWE-770)

locations.role: model-list GET and full JSON materialization

codeEvidence.label: Default mutable alias reaches model resolution
codeEvidence.explanation: The normal online path resolves the configured alias before OCR, and the built-in default is the mutable `mistral-ocr-latest` value.

codeEvidence.label: Model catalog is read without bounds
codeEvidence.explanation: Mutable aliases trigger an authenticated `GET /v1/models`; unrestricted `into_json()` completes before family and stability filtering.

codeEvidence.label: Timeout policy is not connected to HTTP
codeEvidence.explanation: The configuration path accepts the default timeout but explicitly leaves adapter transports unwired, so it does not bound a connected peer's response.

codeEvidence.label: Schema declares a timeout control
codeEvidence.explanation: The public configuration schema declares `timeout_seconds`, establishing the expected operator-controlled deadline that the transport does not enforce.

rootCause.summary: The default `mistral-ocr-latest` alias is resolved by calling `GET /v1/models` and then unrestricted `into_json()`. The documented timeout setting is not wired into the HTTP path, and no compressed or decompressed response limit precedes parsing and model filtering.

remediation: Thread the configured timeout into a shared HTTP client and enforce compressed/decompressed response byte ceilings before parsing the model catalog.

validation.summary: Exact default-alias-to-GET-to-into_json source trace. Cargo.lock pins ureq 2.12.1; local primary source shows connect=30s, read/write/overall=None and unbounded serde_json::from_reader. Bounded network-free r12_2_timeout_seconds_non_default_is_loud_rejected test passed, confirming 30 is rejected and the unwired default 300 accepted.
assertions: Cargo.lock pins ureq 2.12.1; local primary source shows connect=30s, read/write/overall=None and unbounded serde_json::from_reader.
Bounded network-free r12_2_timeout_seconds_non_default_is_loud_rejected test passed, confirming 30 is rejected and the unwired default 300 accepted.
counterevidence: A fixed immutable model bypasses model-list resolution.
Credentials, HTTP status mapping, JSON validity, and post-parse family/stability filtering remain enforced.
limitations: No loopback delay/body measurement was run under the read-only/no-network constraint; exact callsite, explicit configuration comment, and dependency defaults make this non-material to disposition.
No loopback timing or body-size measurement was retained; exact resource thresholds remain unknown.

attackPath.summary: The operator uses the default mutable Mistral model alias in an approved online workflow. KCS performs the authenticated model-list request before OCR. The configured remote endpoint, proxy, or intermediary slow-streams or returns an oversized or compressed model-list body. KCS reads, decompresses, and fully materializes the JSON without a read or overall deadline or byte ceiling before family and stability filtering, hanging the command or consuming substantial memory.

likelihood.why: The mutable default alias is used rather than a fixed immutable model. An online Mistral operation is authorized and a connected remote peer behaves maliciously or incorrectly.

counterevidence: Fixed model pins avoid the vulnerable request.
Connect time is bounded and semantic model filtering prevents adoption of unrelated IDs, but both controls fail to bound a connected peer's read or body.

remediationTests: Drive model resolution through a bounded local fake transport and assert slow reads and oversized compressed/decompressed catalogs fail at configured limits.
Verify immutable model pins bypass catalog retrieval while valid bounded mutable-alias catalogs still resolve correctly.
preventiveControls: HTTP, JSON, model-family, and stability validation after materialization
Thread the configured timeout into a shared HTTP client and enforce compressed/decompressed response byte ceilings before parsing the model catalog.
